Assembly.description:
Intent layer serialisation (DESIGN.md §3, docs/tasks/0006).

An assembly is saved as the record of how it was built, not as geometry:

* ``inlet``: pose (``position``, ``normal``, ``up``) and spec of the first interface (index 0), and ``nozzle`` (drum and nozzle name) for a network started with ``Assembly.from_nozzle``; the drum then sets the pose; * ``edges``: in creation order, each a fitting (``type`` + dataclass fields) with ``source`` (the interface index it was added from), ``close`` (the ``[source, target]`` interfaces it joins), or ``prepend: true`` (placed upstream of the inlet), and its ``label`` if set; * ``names``: interface index → name, for every named interface; * ``equipment``: indices of the interfaces marked as equipment ends (omitted when none); * ``tail``: the interface index ``add(fitting)`` continues from; * ``axial_cell`` if set. Every saved fitting holds its resolved ``n_layers``, so ``axial_cell`` only matters for fittings added after loading.

Replaying the edges recreates the interfaces in the same order, so interface indices are stable. Outlet frames follow from the fittings; only a frame set by hand after ``add()`` is stored, under ``frames``, as an override.

Lengths are in the user's unit and are stored unconverted. Angles are in degrees. :func:`upgrade` converts older versions: version 1 stored ``PipeSpec.rot`` in radians (decision 0024); version 2 used the names from before decision 0053; version 3 saved a profile as a tuple (``["cosine", s0]``). A spec without ``kind`` is concentric.

Input-only fitting fields (``toward``) are resolved by ``Assembly.add()`` and never saved.

axial_cell.description: axial cell size that n_layers=None resolves from

tail.description: the interface the next add continues from

version.description: the description's version; older ones load through intent.upgrade()

Assembly.title: Assembly

Bend.description:
Circular-arc bend whose mesh nodes lie exactly on the true geometry.

A station is placed at every axial layer and stations are joined by circular arcs about the bend axis, so every mesh node lies on a station face or an axial arc and wall nodes are exactly on the torus.

(Exact OCC side surfaces via trimmed revolutions were tried and rejected: OCC fails to trim revolutions of the off-centre inner-square arcs and, at large angles, re-creates boundary curves instead of reusing them.)

angle.description:
turn angle; nonzero (below RADIANS_WARNING_BELOW it is probably radians).

Bend angle in degrees.

axial_grading.description:
ratio of consecutive axial cell lengths, inlet → outlet (1 = uniform).

Ratio of consecutive axial cell lengths, inlet → outlet (1 = uniform; > 1 refines toward the inlet). Stations are spaced accordingly.

n_layers.description:
axial layers; None resolves from the assembly's axial_cell.

Total hex layers along the arc.

radius.description:
centreline radius; above the pipe's outer radius.

Centreline bend radius [m]; must exceed the pipe outer radius.

roll.description:
bend-plane rotation about the inlet axis (0 = toward the inlet's up).

Bend-plane rotation about the pipe axis in degrees (0 = bend toward ``up``).

stack_changes.description:
(i, spec) pairs ending or starting outer layers from axial cell i on (decision 0006).

``(i, spec)`` pairs ending or starting outer layers from axial cell *i* on, as for ``Straight`` (decision 0006).

toward.description:
absolute direction to turn toward, instead of roll (input only: roll is saved).

Absolute direction to turn toward, instead of *roll*: its component across the inlet sets ``roll`` when the bend is added (only ``roll`` is saved).

An input: left out of the description while unset.

Bend.title: Bend

arcs.description:
divisions of each quadrant arc, NE→NW first, instead of n_arc.

Divisions of each quadrant arc, corner *k* → *k* + 1 (NE→NW first), instead of *n_arc* (decision 0041, task 0147). Saved as a list. Four equal counts are the same circle as ``n_arc``. The O-H and H layouts mesh opposite arcs equal only, ``(a, b, a, b)``, which is what meets a rectangle with ``n_width = a``, ``n_height = b``; ``PipeSpec`` rejects other patterns.

n_arc.description:
divisions per quadrant arc, shared by every layer; leave out when arcs is given.

Number of mesh divisions per quadrant arc. Must be identical for every layer in the same pipe stack (conformality requirement).

radius.description:
radius of the circle.

Outer radius of the circle.

Closure.description:
Smooth run between two *existing* interfaces — closes loops.

Only usable through ``Assembly.close()``: both ports are given, so ``ports()`` is undefined. The centreline is a cubic Hermite curve that leaves the source along its normal and arrives at the target along its normal. Stations equidistribute arc length plus turning angle, so sharp turns get more stations. Cross-section frames are parallel-transported (no spurious twist) and the residual roll mismatch — modulo the symmetry period P of the cross-section (90° for a circle or a square, 180° for a rectangle) — is distributed linearly by arc length. A mismatch of exactly P/2 could be absorbed either way and is rejected as ambiguous (DESIGN §8).

axial_grading.description:
ratio of consecutive axial cell lengths, inlet → outlet (1 = uniform).

Ratio of consecutive station spacings, source → target, as for ``SplinePipe``; 1 = uniform.

n_layers.description:
axial layers along the run; None resolves from axial_cell.

Hex layers along the run.

tension.description:
end-tangent magnitude over the chord length.

End-tangent magnitude as a multiple of the chord length. Larger values keep the run straighter near its ends.

Closure.title: Closure

Core.description:
Set the innermost (core) layer.

The shape can be specified either by passing a ``shape`` object directly, or by passing geometry keyword arguments so that the shape is built automatically from the PipeSpec-level division counts:

- Circular core: pass ``radius=<float>`` — requires ``PipeSpec(n_arc=…)`` - Rectangular core: pass ``half_w=<float>, half_h=<float>`` — requires ``PipeSpec(n_width=…, n_height=…)``

Both forms are equivalent::

# explicit shape (old form — still valid): PipeSpec(n_arc=5).core("fluid", shape=CircleShape(0.3, n_arc=5), n_radial=4)

# shorthand (no repeated n_arc): PipeSpec(n_arc=5).core("fluid", radius=0.3, n_radial=4)

layout.description:
section layout (decision 0036).

The section layout (decision 0036): ``"h"``, one Cartesian patch, the default for a rectangular core (since 0.4.0, task 0087); or ``"oh"``, the 5-patch O-H face, the default for a circle and the opt-in for a rectangle. An H core has no ring, so no ``n_radial``; ``radial_grading`` is then the wall growth ratio, the second cell from each wall over the first (> 1 refines toward the walls), and ``first_cell`` its end cell. Both resolve here to ``wall_bump``.

n_radial.description:
O-H radial cells, inner square to wall (0 on an H core).

Radial mesh layers (from inner square to outer boundary).

name.description:
material label of the core.

Material label for the core region.

radial_grading.description:
radial progression (> 1 refines inward); H: wall growth ratio.

Radial progression factor (default 1, uniform; > 1 refines toward the inner square, < 1 toward the outer wall).

shape.description:
the core outline: a circle or a rectangle.

``CircleShape`` or ``RectShape`` describing the core outer boundary. Mutually exclusive with ``radius`` / ``half_w`` / ``half_h``.

wall_bump.description:
an H core's Bump coefficients (c_w, c_h); < 1 refines toward the walls.

An H core's ``Bump`` coefficients, ``(c_w, c_h)``: the sides of ``n_width`` and of ``n_height`` divisions (< 1 refines toward both walls; gmsh's two-sided law). What ``first_cell=`` resolves to, and what ``to_dict`` stores, as O-H stores ``radial_grading``: a k× refinement keeps them, so its nodes nest. ``first_cell=`` and ``radial_grading=`` resolve to it.

Core.title: Core

Drum.description:
Horizontal or vertical drum: a cylinder between two heads.

*diameter* is the inside diameter, *length* the tangent-to-tangent length, *position* the centre of the first tangent plane. *axis* and *up* are normalised, and *up* is made perpendicular to *axis*.

Elbow.description:
Standard butt-weld elbow: a ``Bend`` whose radius follows the pipe.

``schedule="long"`` gives a centreline radius of 1.5 D, ``"short"`` 1 D (ASME B16.9 long- and short-radius elbows), with D the outer diameter of the inlet spec. The radius therefore needs the spec and is resolved in ``ports`` / ``validate``. *roll* and *toward* are as for ``Bend``.

absolute direction to turn toward, instead of roll (input only: roll is saved)

MiterBend.description:
Segmented (mitred) bend: straight pipe pieces joined at planar cuts.

The centreline is the tangent polygon of the smooth bend with the same *radius* and *angle*: ``n_cuts`` cuts each turn ``angle / n_cuts``, the end legs are half segments, and the ports are exactly those of ``Bend(radius, angle, roll=roll)``. Each cut face lies in the plane bisecting its turn; it is the station face stretched into the exact ellipse where the two cylinders meet, so wall nodes on a cut lie on both pipes.

angle.description:
turn angle; nonzero (below RADIANS_WARNING_BELOW it is probably radians).

Total bend angle in degrees.

n_cuts.description:
number of cuts (welds); each turns angle / n_cuts.

Number of cuts (welds); 1 is a single miter joint.

n_layers.description:
axial layers of each end leg (inner segments get twice as many).

Axial layers of each end leg; inner segments, twice as long, get ``2 * n_layers``. Every layer is its own station (see ``path``).

radius.description:
centreline radius of the equivalent smooth bend; above the pipe's outer radius.

Centreline radius of the equivalent smooth bend; must exceed the pipe outer radius (the end legs are ``radius * tan(cut / 2)`` long).

roll.description:
bend-plane rotation about the inlet axis (0 = toward the inlet's up).

Bend-plane rotation about the pipe axis in degrees, as for ``Bend``.

toward.description:
absolute direction to turn toward, instead of roll (input only: roll is saved).

Absolute direction to turn toward, instead of *roll*, as for ``Bend``.

An input: left out of the description while unset.

*axial*: distance of the nozzle axis from the first tangent plane; *angle*: degrees about the drum axis from the drum ``up``; *projection*: distance from the drum axis to the nozzle face.

n_width.description:

Reducer.description:
Concentric reducer (or expander): a straight cone between two radii.

*outlet* is the outlet spec. It must equal the inlet spec in everything except its sizes (every layer's outline: radii, half-widths) and radial gradings (``radial_grading`` per layer): the same layers, outline shapes, ``n_radial``, counts, ``arc_bump``, ``n_outer`` and ``rot``, so that every axial edge joins matching nodes (rule A4; decision 0026). A larger outlet makes it an expander. A rectangle's sides stay planar (the station outlines interpolate linearly), so a duct reducer is exact too. ``Reducer`` changes sizes; ``Transition`` changes shapes.

Every axial layer is a station whose radii interpolate linearly, and corresponding corners are joined by straight lines, which are generators of the cone; wall nodes therefore lie exactly on the cone. Radial gradings interpolate geometrically at the same fractions (``radial_grading_in^(1-u) · radial_grading_out^u``), so a wall-resolved pipe (absolute ``first_cell``) can change diameter (decision 0016). *axial_grading* spaces the stations as for ``Straight``.

*profile* replaces the cone by a radius profile (decision 0008), a :class:`Profile`: ``Profile.cosine(s0)`` (a constriction for s0 > 0, a bulge for s0 < 0), ``Profile.venturi(beta, divergent)`` or ``Profile.table([(s, R/R_in), …])``. Every radius of the stack scales by the profile's ratio, so the outlet must be the inlet scaled by ``r(1)``. Stations lie exactly on R(s); between them the wall is a straight chord, and ``validate`` rejects a chord more than *chord_tol* · R_in from the profile, naming the layers needed.

axial_grading.description: ratio of consecutive axial cell lengths, inlet → outlet (1 = uniform)

chord_tol.description: largest wall-chord gap from the profile, in inlet radii

n_layers.description: axial layers; None resolves from the assembly's axial_cell

outlet.description: outlet spec: the inlet's but for sizes and radial gradings

profile.description: radius profile instead of a cone: Profile.cosine(s0), Profile.venturi(beta, divergent) or Profile.table([(s, R/R_in), …])

Reducer.title: Reducer

Shell.description:
Add a shell: the region between the previous outline and this layer's (decision 0026).

Give exactly one of *dR* (the previous outline grown by *dR*) and *outer* (a new outline, ``CircleShape`` or ``RectShape``). In a stack of rectangles every outline takes the core's ``(n_width, n_height)``, which may differ (decision 0041, option B). A stack with a rectangle and a circle has equal counts on every side of every outline (``n_arc = n_width = n_height``): a circle carries one count. Any stack with a rectangle has ``n_outer`` 4 or 8 (8 cuts the 4-corner face, task 0088). Checked here. That each outline lies inside the next is checked by the assembly's validation.

dR.description:
thickness: the previous outline grown by dR (or outer).

Thickness of this layer.

n_radial.description:
radial cells across the shell.

Radial mesh divisions across the layer.

name.description:
material label of the shell.

Material label.

outer.description:
the shell's outline, instead of dR.

This layer's outline.

radial_grading.description:
radial progression (> 1 refines toward the inner boundary).

Radial progression factor (default 1, uniform; > 1 refines toward the inner boundary, < 1 toward the outer).

type.description: the layer kind; square_shell is the form saved before decision 0026, read as a rect outer

Shell.title: Shell

SplinePipe.description:
Pipe along a cubic spline through *points* (first point = inlet).

The spline leaves the inlet along its normal; it ends along *end_tangent* if given, otherwise with zero curvature. Stations are placed as for ``Closure`` (arc length + turning angle), one axial layer each, with parallel-transported (Bishop) frames, so the outlet roll follows from the curve and every wall node lies on a station circle.

axial_grading.description:
ratio of consecutive axial cell lengths, inlet → outlet (1 = uniform).

Ratio of consecutive station spacings (in arc length + turning angle), inlet → outlet; 1 = uniform.

end_tangent.description:
outlet direction; None leaves the curve free.

Outlet direction (normalised).

n_layers.description:
axial layers (stations) along the curve; None resolves from axial_cell.

Hex layers (= stations) along the curve.

points.description:
curve points, at least two; the first is the inlet position.

At least two distinct consecutive points; ``points[0]`` must be the inlet position.

SplinePipe.title: SplinePipe

Straight.description:
Straight pipe run between two parallel interfaces.

*axial_grading* is the ratio of consecutive axial cell lengths, inlet → outlet (1 = uniform; > 1 refines toward the inlet).

*stack_changes* ends or starts outer layers inside the run (decision 0006): each ``(i, spec)`` gives the stack from axial cell *i* on (``0 < i < n_layers``). ``((3, bare), (7, insulated))`` with ``n_layers=10`` leaves a bare gap of cells 3–6. The outlet port carries the last stack.

*twist* (degrees, either sign) rotates the cross-section about the axis, linearly in the axial distance from inlet to outlet: the outlet's ``up`` is the inlet's rolled by *twist* (decision 0031, task 0062). A twisted run has a station at every axial layer, so every node lies on an exact station face.

axial_grading.description: ratio of consecutive axial cell lengths, inlet → outlet (1 = uniform)

n_layers.description: axial layers; None resolves from the assembly's axial_cell

stack_changes.description: (i, spec) pairs ending or starting outer layers from axial cell i on (decision 0006)

twist.description: rotation of the section about the axis, inlet → outlet, linear along it

Straight.title: Straight

cells along the core block; None resolves from axial_cell.

Cells along the core block (and along the wall). ``None`` resolves from ``Assembly(axial_cell=…)`` over ``length`` minus the cap.

The outlet spec: the same rectangle and counts, the other layout. From an O-H inlet the default is the H face, ungraded; give it to grade the H walls (``first_cell=``, ``wall_bump=``). From an H inlet it is required (it carries ``n_radial`` and the ring's ``radial_grading``).

Pipe tees: the angle in degrees between the run's downstream direction and the branch axis, in (0, 90] (task 0060): 90 is a tee, 45 a 45° lateral leaning downstream. The branch axis passes through the T-point on the main axis; ``branch_length`` is measured along it.

branch_first_cell.description:
pipe tees: the branch port's core wall cell; resolves to branch_radial_grading when added.

The turning station keeps the main's grading, and the branch run's cells blend to the port's over its ``n_branch`` layers. Without them the branch copies the main's ``radial_grading``, so its wall cell scales with r/R. Not on an equal tee or a duct tap.

The turning station keeps the main's grading, and the branch run's cells blend to the port's over its ``n_branch`` layers. Transition.description:
Straight transition that changes outline shapes: a circle to a rectangle, or a rectangle to another (decision 0009, option B; task 0029), in every layer of a stack (decision 0026, task 0046).

*outlet* is the outlet spec. The two are equal in everything but each layer's outline (shape and size): the same layers (names, order, ``n_radial``, grading), equal counts per side throughout (a circle's ``n_arc`` equals a rectangle's ``n_width`` and ``n_height``), ``arc_bump`` and ``rot``. So the two faces have equal signatures (switch class 0) and every axial edge joins matching nodes. A change of sizes only, every outline keeping its shape, is a ``Reducer``; a stack of circles at both ends always is.

Every axial layer is a station whose outlines each blend the two end outlines, point by point at equal arc-length fractions (``core.shape.BlendShape``); a shell's corner lines blend with them, so every layer changes together and the rings stay nested (checked at every station and between them). Wall nodes lie exactly on the station curves; the end stations are the exact end outlines. *axial_grading* spaces the stations as for ``Straight``.

**An H rectangular end** (decision 0036 item 5, task 0085): one end may be an H face (``layout="h"``) with the other end's counts per side. The transition stays a class-0 blend to the O-H face of that rectangle (the other end's ``n_radial`` and ``radial_grading``), and a ``Switch`` takes the slabs at the H end: the fewest of the ``n_layers`` that give it its shortest length (``switch.min_length``) at equal shares of the length. Shells (task 0086): the blend's H-end face carries the H end's shells, which the switch keeps.

A count left ``None`` (the default) is resolved when the wye is added: the fewest layers that keep every edge it divides, the hub cap's arcs included, no longer than the angular cell at the wall, (π/2)·R / ``n_arc``, or ``axial_cell`` if the assembly sets a shorter one (task 0056).
